title: Console: provenance flags and confidence bands for reconstructed per-model usage
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Summary: Some Console charts currently show single-line historical usage after we apply post-hoc corrections (rate-limit retries, quota adjustments, or late ingestion backfills). Those single values obscure provenance and make it hard for operators and customers to trust per-model breakdowns. This ticket adds visible provenance flags (origin tags) and confidence bands for reconstructed points so users can tell which datapoints are final vs. reconstructed/estimated and see uncertainty on aggregated lines.

Problem details:
- Backfilled events and quota corrections can change past token/embedding tallies in per-model charts.
- When we apply corrections, the graph overwrites prior points without any metadata, which hides that the value changed and why.
- Aggregations across models amplify reconstructed variance; SRE and billing ops spend time investigating diffs when customers escalate.

Goals:
1) Surface a compact provenance indicator on charted time-series when any point relies on reconstructed or backfilled events (e.g., a small dot or dashed segment with tooltip explanation).
2) Calculate and render a lightweight confidence band (±X%) for points that are partially reconstructed, based on known uncertainty sources (missing event windows, dedup heuristics, rate-limit retry attribution).
3) Annotate the chart tooltip with a short provenance summary and links to the backfill job / reconciliation job that created the correction.
4) Ensure export/CSV includes provenance and reconstructed-flag columns for downstream analysis.

Approach:
- Telemetry: Add a provenance enum to our timeseries event model upstream (values: original, corrected, reconstructed_estimate, inferred_by_rules). For storage compatibility, store as a separate string tag per timeseries bucket.
- Confidence calculation: Define a simple envelope heuristic: 
  * If point includes >=90% original events -> confidence = high (±2%).
  * If point contains 50–90% original + small reconciled deltas -> confidence = medium (±5–10%).
  * If point is mostly reconstructed/backfilled -> confidence = low (±15–25%).
  Numbers are tunable and recorded in a config table so we can iterate.
- Console UX: chart line rendering layered with a translucent band for confidence and an inline provenance marker for reconstructed ranges. Tooltip lists counts: original_tokens, corrected_tokens, reconstructed_tokens, confidence_percent, correction_job_id.
- Backfill linkage: When a reconciliation job runs, it must emit a correction job id and a small JSON summary into the timeseries metadata. Console will map that id into a human-facing link to the reconciliation run logs.

Trade-offs and decisions so far:
- We will not attempt to present per-token-level probabilistic estimates (too heavy). The envelope heuristic is intentionally conservative and explainable.
- To avoid inflating storage, provenance tags are stored per time-bucket (1h) only; sub-hour precision will be approximated by bucket weighting.
- We chose visual confidence bands over numeric-only flags because ops asked for quick visual triage.

Testing and rollout plan: 
- Unit tests for provenance propagation from ingestion through rollup and aggregation.
- Synthetic test harness: replay a 7-day window with injected delayed events and compare pre/post visuals and CSV exports.
- Canary roll: enable in Console for 10% of orgs and internal Redwood orgs first, with a feature flag controlling band rendering.
- Monitoring: Add an SLO for missing_provenance_tags_rate (<0.1%) and a dashboard for correction_job_link_failures.

Observability/Docs:
- Doc page draft: "Understanding reconstructed usage in Console" with examples and recommended actions for customers who see large reconstructed deltas.
- Internal runbook: steps for investigating reconstructed spikes (dashboards to query, logs to inspect, and common remediation).

Open questions: 
- Exact thresholds for confidence bands (proposal above) — needs validation against historic backfills.
- Does CSV export require separate columns per provenance bucket or a single JSON blob? CSV preferred for downstream BI, but we need to limit column explosion.

Post-mortem linkage: For incidents where we previously scrambled billing reconciliations, we'll attach links and example visual diffs to this ticket so the team can validate UX improvements address operator pain points.
